results.title: Pleased to meet with Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu @atikuabagudu, Minister of Budget & Economic Planning.
results.description:
Pleased to meet with Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu @atikuabagudu, Minister of Budget & Economic Planning. On behalf of the Chinese Government, I signed the Agreement on Development Cooperation with Nigeria, providing RMB 200 million (roughly $30 million) in grant funding.

These funds will focus on "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, characterized by less investment, quick return, fast implementation, and direct public benefit. This grant underscores China’s commitment to aligning our 15th Five-Year Plan with Nigeria's Renewed Hope Agenda, reflecting our enduring strategic partnership, deep mutual trust, strong friendship, and firm solidarity.🇨🇳🇳🇬

results.title: NIGERIA SIGNS $30M DEVELOPMENT GRANT AGREEMENT WITH CHINA.
results.description:
NIGERIA SIGNS $30M DEVELOPMENT GRANT AGREEMENT WITH CHINA.

Nigeria and China have signed a 200-million-yuan agreement, worth approximately US$30 million, to finance small-scale development projects across Nigeria.

Chinese Ambassador Yu Dunhai described the proposed interventions as “small but beautiful” projects designed to deliver practical results and improve people's livelihoods.

Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Abubakar Bagudu said:

• State governments have submitted project proposals.
• The proposals will be reviewed and consolidated.
• Nigeria and China will jointly identify projects for funding.
• The initiative is intended to address local development needs.
Importantly, the $30 million is a grant, not a commercial loan.
However, the specific projects, beneficiary communities and implementation timetable have not yet been announced.
The real measure of success will be whether the money translates into completed projects that Nigerians can see and benefit from.

Which communities and projects should receive priority?

results.title: OPay’s $19 US IPO Faces Setback as US Investors Question Valuation, Nigerians Compare Dangote’s Share Offer OPay’s planned $304 million init
results.description:
OPay’s $19 US IPO Faces Setback as US Investors Question Valuation, Nigerians Compare Dangote’s Share Offer

OPay’s planned $304 million initial public offering (IPO) in the United States has suffered a major setback after indications emerged that investors were unwilling to meet its proposed $19-per-share price.

The Chinese-backed Nigerian fintech company had planned to offer approximately 16 million American Depositary Shares (ADSs) on the New York Stock Exchange, allowing American investors to acquire stakes without directly accessing Nigeria’s stock market.

However, reports indicated that prospective investors were offering between $16.25 and $16.75 per share, considerably below the proposed $19 price.

OPay subsequently suspended the offering, citing an outstanding regulatory inquiry in an undisclosed foreign jurisdiction.

The development has triggered discussions among Nigerians, with many comparing OPay’s proposed dollar-denominated share offer with Dangote Refinery’s share offering in Nigeria.

While Dangote's shares were offered at ₦525 each, OPay's proposed $19 price translated to approximately ₦25,650 at an exchange rate of ₦1,350 to the dollar.

Some commentators have questioned whether OPay overestimated its valuation by targeting American investors instead of testing demand in its home market.

The setback has also reignited conversations about corporate valuation, investor confidence and the importance of understanding market expectations before launching a public offering.

OPay has not confirmed that pricing concerns caused the suspension.
